cards.title: When a card earns its place, and how deep cards may nest
cards.block: Foundations > Visual language > Grouping > Containers (Components > Card)
cards.default: (default + heuristic) On wide layouts, group with space first. On compact widths, cards may be the main way to group. Never put a visible card inside a visible card: group the inside with space. Every card must do something; merge or remove the rest [S-L19-061] [S-L19-068]. This **differs from DC-L15-05**, whose lint allows two container levels. The sources support one card level, so the proposal is `maxCardDepth: 1` as a warning, not a block, because [S-L19-053] says nesting is sometimes unavoidable. Q-dir-04's current use/avoid line already says to avoid nesting containers inside containers, so this tightens the lint, not the guidance.

cards.title: How list rows are separated
cards.block: Foundations > Visual language > Grouping > Lists (and Foundations > Borders > Dividers)
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Separate list rows with space. Use an alternating tint when rows must sit tight (compact density, dense tables). Use lines only when the product's style is built on lines. For a dense list, add differentiation (group headers, avatars, icons) before adding space. This also confirms DC-L15-04: denser layouts need stronger grouping. This **differs from DC-L04-08 and DC-L15-05**, which default to lines for dense or long lists. The preference for space and zebra comes from one video [S-L19-070], and [S-L19-047] offers all three without choosing, so keep `lines` as an equal option for data tables and change only the default wording for lists [inferred].

cards.title: Edge-built alignment inside compact components
cards.default: (default + heuristic) In compact components, every element touches at least two edges; labels align to the start and values to the end. When something floats, manufacture an edge before hiding it in a menu. cards.title: Padding grows with the container
cards.block: Foundations > Space > Semantic spacing > Inset scale
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Padding grows with the container: pick the inset step from the container's size (chip xs, card sm or md, section media xl [inferred mapping]). A group of snug cards uses a gap equal to their inset. Both rules rest on one designer's build [S-L19-103], with [S-L19-060] agreeing only that grouped cards sit close with precise spacing, so they are a recommended heuristic, not a lock. Chips squish to a half or a quarter. This confirms `4-grid-8-rhythm` and the `hybrid` scale. Large values stay on the scale's steps rather than being rounded to 5 or 10, because hand-typed values break STD-visual-details-26 [inferred].

cards.title: Priority placement on work surfaces and dashboards
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Rank modules before placing them. The top row holds page actions; high-priority modules go at the top start; every module keeps the same margins. If the same module appears on two pages, one of them is probably wrong [inferred from S-L19-061].

cards.title: Moving a multi-panel screen to a phone
cards.default: (default + heuristic) On compact widths, give each screen one job: keep the highest-priority panel and move the others to their own pages. Each section flows in one direction. Type and component spacing never shrink below the desktop values. Heuristic: if a section needs two directions on a phone, split it into two sections or two pages.

cards.title: Variety between sections on marketing pages
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Vary: no two sections of one page share a layout. That strict form is one video's practice [S-L19-082]; the other sources ask for variety without a hard rule ([S-L19-065], [S-L19-085], [S-L19-072], [S-L19-073]), so the builder should warn, not block. Break the box only in small, nameable ways, and at most one well-built surprise per page. The count of one is inferred from "once in a while" [S-L19-084], and the surprise is tested before it ships (STD-visual-details-37). None of this applies to product screens. Choosing different familiar section patterns is variety, not breaking a pattern [inferred].

cards.title: Choosing a section pattern by item count and amount of content
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Pick the pattern by item count and content amount. Three to five detailed items: stacked cards or tabs. About 3 to 10 comparable items: a carousel. Many features that would run off the screen: a bento [S-L19-043]. More than about 10: a different format, such as a grid or a separate page [inferred; S-L19-060 says only that another format may be better]. A single statement: a text-only section with three or more lines. All counts are opinion from one video [S-L19-060]; no other source or card gives numbers.

cards.title: How a bento grid is built
cards.default: (default + heuristic) A simple bento on the page's column grid (tiles span whole columns), sized after the content plan. If a tile has nothing real to show, fall back to a plainer layout. This confirms DC-L15-07 (a bento is a hierarchical grid for marketing features) and DC-L03-15's columns.

cards.title: How long pages separate their sections
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Separate sections with space by default. Add background bands for rhythm on long pages [inferred; S-L19-085 says they separate sections and add depth]. Use a frame of lines or a canvas grid only as a deliberate style, mainly when there are no custom graphics [S-L19-103]. Avoid lines as a substitute for spacing [S-L19-050] (one video's taste, which it says is softening). Strip tints and background cards that do nothing [S-L19-103].

cards.title: What a card shows first, what it groups and what it drops
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Rank, group, drop. Each card has one lead fact, grouped secondary facts, and labels only where values could be confused. The card carries what people compare; the detail page carries the rest. This confirms DC-L13-04 (front-load the key information) at card level.

cards.title: Whole-card link or explicit button
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Repeated cards that go to one place are one whole-card link, with a sign that does not depend on hover on touch screens. A card with its own specific action keeps an explicit button, and the card itself stays static. Never combine a card link with competing buttons inside it. Keep hover motion for occasional marketing cards, not for cards people use all day (STD-when-to-animate-07) [inferred link].

cards.title: How a layout is judged before it is chosen
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Show every layout option in the interview full size, in a real frame (a 1920 by about 1,000 px desktop fold and a phone with browser chrome), with realistic content, one at a time. Before a layout is chosen, it should pass the 5-second scroll test [S-L19-084].

cards.title: Corner radius for images, screenshots and chart bars
cards.block: Foundations > Shape > Radius roles > Media and data marks
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Standalone images and screenshots use `radius.media`, which equals `radius.container` [inferred: the sources only say images and buttons must not clash [S-L19-072]; images are container-sized, so DC-L04-03's size rule points to the container step]; images inset in a card use the concentric inner radius; a product screenshot's frame uses the product's own container radius [inferred from S-L19-103]; chart bars are square at the value end; masked shapes appear only on expressive surfaces such as marketing and onboarding [inferred, in line with DC-L06-11]. Rule of thumb: if an image sits next to a button, their corners must visibly come from one family (one presenter, two …

cards.title: Nested corners: pills, wide gaps, flush edges and stacked containers
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Keep DC-L04-05's auto-applied rule and add three cases: (1) pills pass through unchanged; (2) a corner that touches or runs off the container's edge gets 0, with an inset ring on the container when that edge needs definition [S-L19-103]; (3) three radii stacked inside each other are the warning sign that containers nest too deep [S-L19-080]; the nesting limit itself (one visible card level) is DC-L19-42 in the layout area, not repeated here. Rule of thumb: every rounded corner either shares a center with its container's corner or sits flush against it [inferred].

cards.title: Roundness as part of the product's flavor
cards.block: Foundations > Shape > Shape personality > Visual sample
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Keeps the current default of 6px controls and 8-12px containers (DC-L09-01): the sources give no reason to change it, and their one number (10px) is one app's value [S-L19-045]. The link between brand and roundness already exists: Q-brand-01 answers become macros that push the roundness dial (in `levers.json`, playful +30, friendly +15, serious -25, authoritative -20), so Q-shape-01's preselected option already leans with the brand. The sources back that direction [S-L19-043]; nothing new is needed in the engine. When pill is chosen, buttons side by side keep one height [S-L19-103]; making every button a pill rather than a mix is what the video did, and treating it as …

cards.title: Shadow softness, color and strength
cards.block: Foundations > Elevation > Shadow recipe > Softness and color
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Confirms DC-L04-12 (two layers, near-black, alpha 8-24% in light mode). Add four review warnings: x offset at or below y; blur at least 1.3 times y [S-L19-057] (one video's ratio; every research example and the house picker already clear it [inferred]); floating layers cast a stronger shadow than in-page cards [S-L19-052]; bigger surfaces deeper (STD-visual-details-19). In-page cards may drop the shadow entirely [S-L19-045]. Keep the color a see-through near-black rather than a light gray: the house asks for a semi-transparent shadow (STD-visual-details-14, whose point is shadow over solid border) [S-L19-014], and a see-through near-black holds on any background [infer…

cards.title: Bars, toolbars and sheets: see-through layers with a scroll edge
cards.default: (default + heuristic) New web default: nav bars, toolbars and sheets are see-through layers with the sample values, a scroll edge instead of a divider, and both fallbacks generated as CSS media blocks. Glass stays off reading surfaces and product cards (`decorative` stays flagged, DC-L04-15). Blur grows with surface size, but any blur that animates stays under 20px (STD-enter-exit-origin-30): the 20px toolbar sample is fine while it stands still, and a sheet that materializes with blur and scale (STD-enter-exit-origin-31) needs its blur below 20px [inferred]. Differs from DC-L04-15 and DC-L10-12 (opaque on the web); the house standard wins.

cards.title: Which overlays dim the page, and how much
cards.block: Foundations > Opacity > Scrims > When to dim
cards.default: (default + heuristic) The builder decides by component type instead of asking: modal dialogs and blocking drawers (drawers are modal by default, STD-components-toasts-drawers-39) get a 40% near-black scrim in light mode; non-blocking panels get none; each stacked parent dims one more step. Q-depth-06 then asks only about strength. Rule of thumb: dim only when the person must finish or dismiss the layer before going on [S-L19-020].

cards.title: Special surface effects and where they may appear
cards.default: (default + heuristic) None on product screens. Effects are allowed on marketing, onboarding and celebration surfaces, each within its source's own limit: clay for illustrations, metal for card and mockup visuals, the kaleidoscope for cards and stickers (not for buttons whose label must be read, although both videos name buttons [S-L19-058] [S-L19-075]), stickers to break up boxy layouts [S-L19-075] (on marketing pages [inferred]), glass cards as decoration. The tactile button is the only effect that may enter product UI, and only with the `soft` style preset of Q-dir-01, which DC-L15-01 offers with a contrast warning [inferred]. Rule of thumb for all of them, glows included: don't pile effe…

cards.title: One icon library, and no emoji as interface icons
cards.block: Foundations > Iconography > Icon library > Consistency guard
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Confirms DC-L05-01 (one open-source set on the web). Add: DESIGN.md and the AGENTS snippet name the library and forbid emoji as interface icons, because AI tools fall back to emoji [S-L19-086] (one presenter, two videos, who also grants that Notion uses emoji well [S-L19-061]); review warns about emoji in buttons, navigation, cards and headings, while user content such as reactions or page icons a person picks stays allowed [S-L19-061] [inferred scope]; third-party components take their icons from the library [S-L19-090]. The house list of curated libraries (STD-visual-details-55) has no icon entry, so OpenDesigner says so and then recommends from DC-L05-01 and these s…

cards.title: Icon size next to text: never taller than the line
cards.block: Foundations > Iconography > Sizes > Pairing with text
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Keep DC-L05-05's pairs and add a ceiling: an icon is never taller than the line height of the text beside it [S-L19-052], and review flags icons that exceed it. Kole Jain's icon-equals-line-height advice is read as the upper limit, not the target [inferred reconciliation]. Smaller icons carry less detail and larger ones more [S-L19-057]; so custom icons stay simplest at the smallest shipped size (16px, or 12px where Q-icon-04's optional size ships) and extra detail belongs at pictogram sizes (DC-L05-11) [inferred sizes].

cards.title: Explaining icon-only controls: a better icon, a label, then a tooltip
cards.block: Foundations > Iconography > Icon with text > Explaining icons
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Confirms `labels-default` plus `universal-only`. Order of fixes: (1) a universally known icon alone [S-L19-045], still with its accessible name and, on pointer devices, the tooltip that `universal-only` already gives it (DC-L05-07; the video says such icons need nothing else, and keeping DC-L05-07's tooltip is the [inferred] reconciliation); (2) a visible label, a better icon or a telling position; (3) a tooltip only as an extra on pointer devices, never the only explanation [S-L19-080] (in line with DC-L05-07 and NN/g's view that labels should be visible, not hover-only). The delayed tooltip's bouncy easing [S-L19-079] differs from the house tooltip motion, and the ho…

cards.title: Icon color and state, by surface
cards.block: Foundations > Iconography > Color and states > By surface
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Confirms DC-L05-08 in the product: neutral icons, color only for status and data. Add: on marketing surfaces, feature icons may use solid accent colors, one icon per feature, not gradient icons [S-L19-062] [S-L19-082]; every navigation icon needs an active version [S-L19-075], so the library must provide filled versions [inferred, from DC-L05-06's filled-when-selected rule]; inactive icons keep 3:1 [inferred].

cards.title: What the imagery shows: the product, the audience, or nothing
cards.block: Foundations > Imagery > Subject > Product and audience imagery
cards.default: (default + heuristic) When the product has marketing surfaces, default the imagery to real product screenshots (3x, cropped to each feature) plus audience imagery wherever the page says who it is for; avoid an image-less marketing page (one video calls it robotic [S-L19-062]; another adds a screenshot when a page has no other graphics [S-L19-103]). Stock only against the photo brief; high resolution only. Product tools with no marketing surface keep `none`. Two heuristics from the update: pick people the audience that pays can recognize themselves in, which means asking who that is before choosing a style [S-L19-111]; and on a screen that sells (a paywall, a hero), test the main image rathe…

cards.title: How product screenshots are framed
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Schoger's well as the recommended starting frame for marketing screenshots (one video's treatment, not a rule; its values stay open until a second product confirms them): a snug inset for feature cards, a generous one for the hero, cropped to what the text describes. Rule of thumb: frame tight for small features, loose for the one big hero [S-L19-103].

cards.title: Text and controls over images
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Order: text beside the image; if it must sit on the image, a better photo first, then a gradient scrim (not a full overlay), with an optional progressive blur; text never over the focal point (one presenter, two videos [S-L19-043] [S-L19-065]); controls on a dark, blurred background or below the image [S-L19-075]. Test contrast at the lightest region behind the text.

cards.title: How playful the imagery is
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Preselect the point on the scale from Q-brand-01's playful to serious slider: playful leans to blobs, the middle to doodles, serious to realistic imagery (which routes to photography, Q-img-01) [inferred mapping from S-L19-063]. The Q-brand-01 macros in `levers.json` already set an illustration style for product states (`playful`: characters in empty and error states; `serious`: pictograms or none); those stay, and this scale sets only the hero and marketing imagery that the source's examples are about [inferred split]. Then check the preselection against the people who pay: where people appear in the imagery, they must be able to recognize themselves in its style, so …

cards.title: Where avatars appear
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Show avatars next to names wherever a person is the subject of a row (logs, assignees, comments); use the uploaded photo for the profile tab and the account entry, with the initials fallback of DC-L05-18; keep circles for people.

cards.title: What a mascot does: brand moments, a companion, or pressure
cards.block: Foundations > Illustration > Characters > The mascot's job
cards.default: (default + heuristic) `none` unless the brand already has a character, or is playful and consumer-facing; with a mascot, `moments` by default. A companion that reacts to the person's own progress is an explicit choice for consumer and play products [inferred scope]. Rule of thumb: the mascot may cheer, celebrate and grow with the person, and never sulks, scolds or threatens (both sides are in [S-L19-105]; drawing the line there is [inferred], in line with DC-L19-37). Check its look against who pays (DC-L19-75): cartoonish characters can miss an older paying audience [S-L19-111].

cards.title: How an AI helper is pictured
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Keep `agent-shape`: a mark of its own, never the person circle, with a neutral voice (DC-L05-18, DC-L13-16). A realistic persona is an explicit choice for products whose AI gives personal guidance, and then only with the AI label always beside it and a shape or badge that sets it apart from people [inferred conditions]. One app's result [S-L19-111] does not outweigh the research, so its caution holds. Rule of thumb: people never have to guess whether they are dealing with a person or an AI [inferred from DC-L13-16 and STD-visual-details-36].

cards.title: Whether images change for each person
cards.default: (default + heuristic) The same images for everyone, with a default set always present. When onboarding already asks about goals, one image set per stated goal on the paywall and onboarding is worth testing, once the screen's design itself has been tested [S-L19-106]; an avatar may use a trait the person chose [S-L19-111]. Never generate product images from the person's own face [S-L19-111] (one app; STD-visual-details-41, ask for private data only when needed, and STD-visual-details-45, cut a feature whose risk outweighs its value, point the same way [inferred]).

cards.title: Which interactions get no motion (the frequency gate)
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Gate on. Tier every component in the inventory; ship no animation on 100+/day and keyboard-initiated actions; expect to reject most motion ideas (at most 5-7 suggestions for a whole app [S-L19-024]). Rule of thumb: the more often it is seen, the less it moves; when unsure, delete the animation [S-L19-032].

cards.title: Motion personality (amount and character)
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default by audience: `playful` when Q-aud-02 is `play`; `crisp` in every other case, including Q-scope-06 `operate` and Q-aud-02 `work` (today's defaults) and `consumer`; Q-aud-02 `high-trust` always caps at `crisp`, as today's cap does at `productive`; `elegant` is offered to anyone but never chosen by default [inferred]. The Mobbin polish argument does not move the `consumer` default: a consumer product that wants to compete on polish keeps `crisp` everyday motion and spends the polish in named delight moments (DC-L19-83), which is where both Mobbin videos put it [S-L19-104] [S-L19-107] [inferred]. Rule of thumb: personality changes how many things move and a compone…

cards.title: Where the delight budget goes (rare moments)
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Pick a few named rare moments (1-3 [inferred]; no source gives a count): first run and milestones by default, plus first-use empty states and the 404 page where the product has them; never a component people use daily. In a product with a daily routine, the daily completion gets standard confirmation and the celebration waits for the milestone [inferred from S-L19-105 and STD-when-to-animate-09]; an everyday work tool gets no surprise motion to keep it "engaging" (STD-when-to-animate-20). Motion on a one-off offer may be a standard entrance or a designed delight moment, never motion added to pull attention; an attention haptic and anything that fakes chance are out. Ru…

cards.title: How lively the marketing pages may be
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default `few-moving-parts` for conversion sites (Q-scope-06 `persuade`); `scroll-story` only for awareness or experience sites. Rules of thumb: the layout should look good before any animation is added [S-L19-082]; motion should point at the product [S-L19-084]; repeat one or two motion themes rather than one-off effects [S-L19-062] (Kole's view across videos, practitioner opinion). Scroll reveals fire once, 100px into view.

cards.title: Easing curves grouped by job
cards.default: (default + heuristic) The job-based set above. Ask: is it entering or leaving, moving on screen, a hover or color change, or constant? If none fits, use ease-out. Differs from DC-L04-21 and DC-L04-24, which give exits an accelerate curve.

cards.title: Duration budget per element
cards.default: (default + heuristic) The per-element budget. Rule of thumb: if it is UI and over 300ms, name the reason (a drawer, a toast's personality) or cut it to 150-250ms. Differs from DC-L04-20 (steps up to 700ms, exits 20-35% shorter).

cards.title: What drives each motion: timing curve, spring or keyframes
cards.block: Foundations > Motion > Motion driver and interruptibility
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Use a spring if a finger was involved and timing for everything else [S-L19-016]. The web house sources add two more spring cases: decorative mouse-tracking values go through a spring (`useSpring`, STD-springs-gestures-45), and so may an element meant to feel alive, such as a Dynamic Island-style morph [S-L19-018] [S-L19-023]. Anything that can fire twice in a second uses transitions, not keyframes. Nothing locks input.

cards.title: Spring parameters and presets
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Four presets plus a clamped dismiss, as above. Rule of thumb: bounce only when a finger threw it; nothing that appears on its own overshoots. Differs from DC-L04-22 (stiffness stored, energy-driven damping, under-damped hero moves) and from Q-motion-04's 0.15 step.

cards.title: How things appear and leave
cards.default: (default + heuristic) The house recipe set. Rule of thumb: everything that enters gets opacity 0 plus a small transform; anything anchored to a trigger grows from it; modals grow from the center; everything leaves the way it came.

cards.title: Screen and page transitions
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Platform default on native, configured through native stack options and never rebuilt in JavaScript; no animation on tab switches and core navigation; on the web, a continuity transition only for occasional drill-ins (card to detail) and onboarding, while on native the same idea stays inside one screen (a card expanding in place) [inferred]; forward moves sideways, temporary things come from the bottom [inferred from S-L19-084 and DC-L04-23].

cards.title: Stagger for groups of items
cards.default: (default + heuristic) 50ms on the web and 40ms in React Native, only for occasionally seen groups and for results the person asked for and is waiting on. Rule of thumb: if they scroll past it all day, it should already be there.

cards.title: What reduced motion does
cards.default: (default + heuristic) `replace`, with a 200ms `ease` cross-fade, shipped with each animation. Rule of thumb: remove travel, keep meaning.

cards.title: Press feedback
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Tint plus a 0.97 scale on every pressable. Rule of thumb: respond the instant the finger lands, within 160ms.

cards.title: Hover motion
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Product UI: color on `ease`, and subtle reveals only for secondary actions; rich hovers only on marketing surfaces. Rule of thumb: the more often it is hovered, the less it moves; if a hover flickers, animate a child instead of the hovered parent.

cards.title: Confirmation and loading motion
cards.block: Patterns > Feedback > Action confirmation and loading motion
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Respond within 50ms (DC-L13-01) with a state change first; add a small confirming motion only where the result is off-screen or invisible (copy, save elsewhere); a fast, linear spinner in the pressed button for waits; a skeleton shimmer for region loads; in long first-run flows, loading and verification steps always show a moving indicator instead of a still screen, as state motion rather than delight [inferred from S-L19-107 and STD-when-to-animate-08]; celebration only for rare successes.

cards.title: Performance budget and the device that proves it
cards.default: (default + heuristic) 60fps on the slowest device named in the proposed Q-plat-11 (Q-plat-02 names only device classes), 120fps where supported, checked on a release build before motion counts as done. Rule of thumb: if an effect needs a preloader to hide its weight, question the effect [inferred from S-L19-040 and S-L19-069].

cards.title: Gestures: which ones, how they commit, and their visible alternative
cards.block: Patterns > Gestures > Drag, swipe and release
cards.default: (default + heuristic) The momentum model is locked; every gesture has a visible button or menu that does the same job; sequential snap points only when every point matters. Rule of thumb: a flick should be enough, and a person who never swipes should still get everything done.

cards.title: Haptics for each moment
cards.default: (default + heuristic) The per-moment map for custom interactions and system haptics for standard controls; one haptic per action; no haptic to draw attention to an offer or to anything the person did not do. Sound stays off by default (Q-motion-08 `silent`); a product built around a routine may add one short completion sound under `rare-events` [S-L19-105] [inferred]. Rule of thumb: vibrate on the moment something catches or completes, never while it moves and never to sell.

cards.title: Motion token structure: shared transitions or component recipes
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Primitives (three curves plus `ease` and `linear`) and component recipes for press, tooltip, dropdown or popover, modal with backdrop, drawer or sheet, toast, accordion and stagger; springs and gesture numbers in `$extensions`; the `energy` dial changes personality and scope (DC-L19-82), never recipe values. Rule of thumb: if two components have different budgets, they need different recipes.

cards.title: Which library supplies each standard part
cards.block: Components > Implementation > Base library (one library per job)
cards.default: (default + heuristic) for React web, `curated-per-job` on top of `keep-installed`. Heuristic: Q-comp-01 picks the approach (headless, copy-in, native, adopt), then the curated list names one library per job in one sentence, never a menu [inferred combination of Q-comp-01 and S-L19-029]. Drawers are built on the chosen dialog primitive with Vaul's behaviours (DC-L19-115).

cards.title: What a control does the moment it is pressed
cards.default: (default + heuristic) `scale-and-tint`: 0.97 plus a darker tint, within 100-160ms ease-out on the web (the engine's 100ms `motion.duration.micro`). The pressed look appears on pointer-down and the action commits on release. Heuristic: the more often a control is pressed, the subtler its feedback (STD-when-to-animate-07).

cards.title: Hover on controls, product screens versus marketing pages
cards.default: (default + heuristic) product UI uses `color-shift`, instant or near-imperceptible, and gated to fine pointers. `rich-motion` is for marketing calls to action only, with one kind per page [inferred]. Heuristic: the more often something is hovered, the less it moves.

cards.title: Emphasis inside a group of buttons
cards.block: Components > Button > Variants; Patterns > Actions > Emphasis
cards.default: (default + heuristic) confirms `four-danger` with one filled button per area. Heuristic: when two actions compete, remove the lesser one's fill (ghost) before adding another style, and make the nav call to action one control size smaller than the hero's [inferred from S-L19-057 and S-L19-103]. When the one filled button commits the person to something, its label says what, and the choice is A/B tested where the product can test it [S-L19-105] [S-L19-104].

cards.title: How visible secondary actions are
cards.block: Patterns > Actions > Disclosure; Components > Icon button, Tooltip, Menu
cards.default: (default + heuristic) place each action by how important and how frequent it is (the spectrum) [S-L19-056]. The product's key action gets a label; secondary actions get icons with tooltips. Use `hover-reveal` only for minor, repeated actions, and only when the same action also shows on focus and has a visible touch fallback [inferred]. Try re-aligning a crowded card before reaching for an overflow menu [S-L19-080].

cards.title: What "on", selected and active look like
cards.default: (default + heuristic) an indicator plus color, with color only on the on or selected state and neutral off states. Brand color on selected items is fine in navigation-light products such as a tab bar. In action-dense products, keep DC-L08-14's neutral selection so the brand color keeps meaning "act" [inferred reconciliation of S-L19-075 and DC-L08-14].

cards.title: Which button carries the fill in a delete confirmation
cards.block: Patterns > Destructive confirmation; Components > Button > Danger
cards.default: (default + heuristic) confirms Q-state-06's default: subtle danger in context, and solid red only in the final confirmation step (DC-L08-06). In that step Delete is the solid red danger button (red, never the brand color [S-L19-051]) and Cancel stays unfilled, so the brand's primary fill never lands on a destructive button (DC-L08-06, DC-L13-18). New: initial focus and Enter go to Cancel [inferred; reconciles S-L19-057's red Delete with S-L19-044's trust in the safe choice]. `safe-fill` stays an option for products that follow the macOS convention. Heuristic: each fill color means the same thing in every dialog (STD-visual-details-36) [S-L19-044].

cards.title: How irreversible actions are guarded
cards.default: (default + heuristic) confirms `both`: undo for reversible actions, confirmation for irreversible ones. New: `hold-to-confirm` as the in-place guard when an irreversible action should not open a dialog (for example from a list row) [inferred]; `slide-to-confirm` only for high-impact actions on touch, with a button fallback.

cards.title: What a pressed control shows while it works and when it is done
cards.block: Components > States > Pending and success; Patterns > Feedback
cards.default: (default + heuristic) press feedback at once (DC-L19-102); a pending state in the button for waits (Q-state-08's timing ladder); `success-in-place` for actions with no visible result; `toast.promise` for work that finishes after the person has moved on; `optimistic` only when failure is rare and reversible (Q-state-08). Heuristic: every action ends in one of three things: pending, success in place, or a toast [inferred from STD-visual-details-49].

cards.title: Text field anatomy and phone input rules
cards.block: Components > Text field; Patterns > Forms > Field anatomy
cards.default: (default + heuristic) confirms `outlined` with top labels. New: the placeholder holds a realistic example, input text is 16px on coarse pointers even when Q-type-08 picks a 14px body, and each field type sets its keyboard attributes.

cards.title: When forms check answers
cards.default: (default + heuristic) inline on blur for every rule the browser can check, not only formats, with errors cleared on the fixing keystroke. Submit-time checks are a backstop only, for server-side errors and untouched required fields, with a summary on forms of more than about 5 fields. **Differs from DC-L08-17's on-submit default;** the house standard decides it. Live checks only for meters and requirement checklists, which show what is met rather than what is wrong [inferred]. A sign-up longer than a few fields may go one step per screen, with each Next checking that step [S-L19-107] [inferred].

cards.title: When a toast is the right channel
cards.default: (default + heuristic) keep `inline-banner` as the default channel. Use toasts (Sonner) for three jobs: confirming a change made in an overlay, reporting work that finishes later, and carrying Undo. A toast with an action gets `duration: Infinity` per call (Sonner's way to persist a toast [S-L19-089]) and stays dismissible, which satisfies DC-L08-18 while plain toasts keep the 4s default; STD-components-toasts-drawers-15 now states this exception itself, and STD-components-toasts-drawers-26 allows the per-call override. An error that blocks progress also appears in place (DC-L13-09).

cards.title: Where toasts sit and how they look
cards.block: Components > Toast > Placement, stack and style
cards.default: (default + heuristic) bottom-right; neutral colors unless Q-color-15 asks for colored status toasts; theme-following; a collapsed stack of 3 that expands on hover; 32/16px offsets; a headless custom toast for the design system.

cards.title: Popover, modal, sheet or new page
cards.block: Patterns > Modality; Components > Popover, Dialog, Sheet
cards.default: (default + heuristic) the ladder. A popover for simple, non-blocking settings and rarely used features; a modal for short tasks tied to the page; a sheet on phones for anything that would be a modal on desktop; a side sheet only when the task needs the page in view and has enough content to fill the panel [inferred from S-L19-061]; a new page for large or lasting context, once existing overlays have been ruled out. Teaching goes into a persistent checklist or the empty state, not a pop-up [S-L19-056] [S-L19-107]; every blocking layer shows its close control from the start [inferred from STD-accessibility-motion-24].

cards.title: How a phone sheet rests and leaves
cards.block: Components > Sheet and drawer > Heights and dismissal
cards.default: (default + heuristic) one height fitted to the content; modal; dismissible by drag, flick, outside click and Escape; plus a visible close or confirm control. Use snap points only for content people browse while keeping context (maps, lists over content), sequential when each point matters equally, and at most three detents on native.

cards.title: What happens to the page behind an overlay
cards.block: Foundations > Depth > Scrim; Components > Sheet and dialog > Backdrop
cards.default: (default + heuristic) `dim-and-push-back` for modal tasks, because STD-visual-details-20 (a house standard) pairs a modal task with a dimming scrim and pushes the background back or down, and stacked sheets dim and push back each parent. The sources show the push-back on phone sheets [S-L19-005] [S-L19-053] [S-L19-035]; the standard does not limit it to them, and the sources give no scale, so a centered desktop dialog may use a very small one picked by eye [inferred]. `no-scrim` for non-blocking panels. `dim` alone is offered only as a recorded override of STD-visual-details-20. (Revised 2026-09-28: the earlier default made the push-back an opt-in, which contradicted the standard.)

cards.title: A command menu, and how it opens
cards.default: (default + heuristic) `none` for simple sites and phone-first apps; `command-menu` (cmdk) for desktop or web tools used daily with more destinations or actions than the sidebar shows [inferred]; `floating-search` for one-screen utilities. It always opens with no animation, and so does whatever a shortcut triggers.

cards.title: What goes in the sidebar, and in what order
cards.block: Components > Side navigation; Patterns > App shell
cards.default: (default + heuristic) `account-top` for multi-account or team products; `logo-top` for single-account products [inferred]. Always: an icon plus a short label, grouped by relevance, settings and help at the bottom, one clear active indicator, collapsible to icons, and counts only when they call for action [inferred reconciliation of S-L19-047 and S-L19-061].

cards.title: The phone tab bar and where the main action goes
cards.block: Components > Tab bar (bottom navigation); Patterns > Navigation > Mobile
cards.default: (default + heuristic) three or four tabs; labels unless every icon is universal; an active state on every tab; the main action inline, unless it is the product's most-used job, in which case break it out [inferred reconciliation of S-L19-053 and S-L19-075]; no animation when switching tabs.

cards.title: Tables and lists: the data picks the display form
cards.block: Patterns > Data display > Tables, lists and activity logs
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default for a `data` product: numbers right-aligned with tabular digits, fixed-value fields as labelled chips, truncation with the full value on hover and focus, shaded inactive rows, bulk actions on multi-select, and search, filter and sort on any table longer than one screen [inferred threshold]. Heuristic, "let the data drive the form": a fixed set of values becomes a chip, a number is right-aligned, records ordered by time are tried as a timeline, a list that can pass 1,000 rows is virtualized. The form rules come from Kole Jain videos only. Virtualization is a house standard (STD-performance-properties-17). Tabular digits are a house standard for price columns and…

cards.title: How charts are drawn on product dashboards
cards.block: Foundations > Data visualization > Chart presentation (product dashboards)
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default: the current `core-6` plus a KPI big number (confirms DC-L05-22 and Q-viz-01), drawn with recharts on the web, with an axis, grid lines, labelled numbers, a legend when there is more than one series, a time-range switch when the data is over time, and no entrance animation on data. Heuristic: one representation per dataset, and "if the chart needs its caption to be read, fix the chart" [inferred]. Straight segments and square bar tops are defaults a brand may change, not lint errors: "no smoothing" comes from two videos by one creator (the finance redesign points back to the other [S-L19-068]), "no rounded tops" from a third [S-L19-045], and the research does n…

cards.title: How visible each action is (the spectrum of explicitness)
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Rank each action by how often it is used and how much it matters, then place it: main and frequent actions labelled and always visible; secondary actions in tight space as icons revealed on hover and focus, with a touch fallback; infrequent features in a popover or menu; advanced options collapsed; tools that need content hidden until content exists. Every icon-only control gets a tooltip. This extends DC-L13-03 (which covers how options are disclosed) to where each action lives, and agrees with its "never hover-only for essentials". The source never covers touch or keyboard for hover reveals, so the fallback rule is [inferred] from DC-L13-03 and STD-accessibility-moti…

cards.title: Which surface a task opens in: popover, modal, sheet or new page
cards.block: Patterns > Modality > Surface by task size and permanence
cards.default: (default + heuristic) A size-and-permanence ladder: popover for simple, non-blocking settings; modal for a short task tied to the page, confirmed by a toast after it closes; side sheet when people must see the page while they edit (DC-L08-20); new page, with a back button or breadcrumb, for permanent or large context; bottom sheet on phones for in-context side tasks. This confirms DC-L08-20 (dialog for short decisions, side sheet for editing with context, bottom sheet on phones) and adds the popover and new-page rungs and the permanence test. It differs slightly from DC-L08-20 on one case: [S-L19-047] puts link creation in a modal because it relates to the list on the page, a task DC-L08-20…

cards.title: Which states every screen and flow ships with
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Scaffold all four states for every collection and every async action, and warn when a flow ships without its success, error and empty variants. That warning is the L13 research's Peak-End lint, which was marked [inferred] there and now has direct source support [S-L19-044] and a house standard behind it (STD-visual-details-49). Heuristic: for each screen, ask "what does it look like with nothing in it, while it waits, when it worked, and when it failed?"

cards.title: Empty states: first use against no results
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Confirms DC-L13-10's kinds and its three jobs (say what is going on, help people learn, give one direct action). Adds: first use shows one focused action with one short explanation, not a grid of invitations; tools that need content (filters, sort, bulk actions) stay hidden until content exists; no results means acknowledge, suggest (a typo fix, clear filters) and offer a way out. Motion: a first-use empty state is rare enough for delight (STD-when-to-animate-09), but an empty state people hit every day, such as inbox zero or a filter with no matches, stays subtle (STD-when-to-animate-04) [inferred split]. The same split settles the all-done state: after a completion p…

cards.title: What people see while they wait, and when to show the result before the server answers
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Proposed default for Q-state-08 (today null): answer on pointer-down; no indicator under about 1 s; a skeleton for page or region loads; a spinner inside the trigger for actions; determinate progress with cancel past 10 s (DC-L13-01); and optimistic updates for likely, reversible actions (delete, move, save), with undo or a rollback message if the request fails. Never optimistic for payments or anything irreversible [inferred from STD-visual-details-40 and DC-L13-01]. Spinners spin fast and linear (STD-easing-duration-15, STD-easing-duration-01). Two small conflicts: [S-L19-045] grays out the pressed button, while DC-L08-12 keeps loading buttons focusable, so gray the …

cards.title: Where confirmations, warnings and errors appear: inline, banner or toast
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Keep `inline-banner` as the default. Routing rule that settles the disagreement between [S-L19-047] and DC-L13-09: an error that blocks progress appears inline at its cause; a warning or error from background work (a failed sync, a failed save after an optimistic update) may use `toast.error`, which answers the concern that such messages get missed [inferred], and the item it concerns also shows its failed state in place wherever it is on screen (DC-L19-112: an error toast only echoes an error shown in place); a change confirmed after a modal closes gets a toast; async actions get one promise toast, never a new toast per state. Plain toasts auto-close after 4000 ms; to…

cards.title: Onboarding: how new users learn the product and get set up
cards.block: Patterns > Guidance > Onboarding and first run
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default `sequenced-tips`: one tip on the main action, then a checklist that stays until setup is done, together with first-use empty states. Two channels now agree on checklists and in-context help over pop-ups ([S-L19-056]; [S-L19-107] with Mural's figure), which confirms DC-L13-11 and turns its "contextual help" into a sequence. Choose `none` when first use is the value [S-L19-107]. Setup: name the aha moment first, ask only what changes what the person sees next, show what each answer unlocked, and allow more than one goal [S-L19-107] [S-L19-111]; judge the flow by how fast it reaches value, never by its screen count [S-L19-107]. Ask for an account when the product …

cards.title: Where the delight budget is spent
cards.block: Foundations > Brand > Expression > Hero moments (by pattern)
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Keep Q-brand-04's default `hero-moments` and name the moments: the welcome screen after sign-up, the first-use empty state, the completion of a rare and meaningful task (a first project published, a milestone), and the 404 page. Heuristic: ask how often this person will see it (STD-when-to-animate-04). Tens of times a day means no delight (a "copied" confirmation stays subtle, STD-when-to-animate-07); once, or at a milestone, means it is eligible. DC-L06-03 sets "one or two hero moments" and DC-L04-19 "1-3 hero moments per flow", but their examples (opening a page, the primary action) recur far more often than STD-when-to-animate-09 allows; DC-L19-83 records that confl…

cards.title: Marketing visuals: show the real product
cards.default: (default + heuristic) For a software product with a marketing page: use the real product. A cropped or crafted product view in the hero, a cropped screenshot per feature, site grays matched to the product. Audience imagery may sit beside the product views where the page says who it is for [S-L19-062]; images unrelated to the product or its users never [S-L19-072]. Four videos agree on showing the product (three by Kole Jain [S-L19-061] [S-L19-072] [S-L19-084], one by Steve Schoger [S-L19-103]); no research card covers product imagery on marketing pages [checked L05 cards DC-L05-14 to DC-L05-21]. The nearest is DC-L05-20, where Atlassian's in-product onboarding illustrations use low-fidelity…

cards.title: Calls to action on marketing pages
cards.block: Patterns > Marketing page > Call to action
cards.default: (default + heuristic) One filled primary action per hero; any second action unfilled; the nav and hero buttons share a label when they share a destination; every long page ends with a call-to-action section, which is required when the hero has none. For prompt or search products, the input is the call to action. Never make a hover-revealed call to action the only way forward. This confirms DC-L13-18; "one primary" appears in two Kole Jain videos and in DC-L13-18, so it is treated as a rule rather than one creator's opinion.

cards.title: How much motion marketing pages get
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default "convert" (DC-L19-84's `few-moving-parts`): motion that points at the product, scroll reveals that fire once on entry (STD-enter-exit-origin-27, STD-enter-exit-origin-28), one well-built signature interaction, no scrolljacking, and a preloader only when heavy media must load, kept short. Choose "remember" (`scroll-story`) only when the page's goal is awareness or Q-scope-06 is `experience`. Heuristic: first "is this page built to convert or to be remembered?" [S-L19-040], then "what does this effect point at?" (STD-when-to-animate-03). Marketing and explanatory motion may run past the 300 ms and 1 s caps (STD-easing-duration-06, STD-easing-duration-09), which c…

cards.title: Pricing pages and plan pickers
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Web pricing page: three or four plans, one of them suggested; the price larger than the name; the real discount and the billing terms under the price; what the next plan adds; Enterprise as a small link on each plan (still visible, so not hidden in the deceptive-pattern sense [inferred]). In-app paywall: two plans, the one that suits the business preselected (yearly, by the source's reasoning), the rest one tap away behind "view all plans" [S-L19-104] [S-L19-106]. Whatever unit is shown large, the billed amount and period are always on screen. The two surfaces differ, they do not contradict: all plans stay reachable, so the two-plan paywall is disclosure, not a cap, wh…

cards.title: Paywalls, upsells and re-engagement prompts
cards.block: Principles > Ethics > Monetization and engagement prompts
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Confirms Q-pattern-05's default `enforced`. Upgrade prompts appear at the limit, say what the next plan adds, and accept one dismissal that sticks (no re-prompting, the DSA example in DC-L13-15). Plan the paywall's moments (after onboarding, a gated feature, settings, cancel), but make every one the same offer that unlocks everything [S-L19-111] [S-L19-104] [inferred reconciliation]. Premium features may be locked, but the paywall itself always has a visible way out, from its first frame, back to whatever is free [inferred application of STD-visual-details-33 and STD-accessibility-motion-24]; so OpenDesigner does not recommend a hard paywall or a delayed close, even wh…

cards.title: Progress, streaks and rewards
cards.default: (default + heuristic) `none` for work tools; `progress` for products built around the person's own goals; a streak or a game or social layer only with an explicit goal, and then with these conditions: optimism or a visible chain as the lever, never fear or guilt [S-L19-105] (DC-L19-37); one unit of the core action keeps the streak alive; freezes, repairs or grace days built in [S-L19-105]; the milestone is celebrated and the daily completion only confirmed (DC-L19-83); rewards tie to real goals and value is shown before any game [S-L19-078]; reminders and other engagement features have an off switch [inferred, generalising the three off switches in S-L19-048]; progress is honest, with no ar…

cards.title: Measuring whether a design change worked
cards.default: (default + heuristic) For `persuade` screens and paywalls, record the one number each major change is meant to move, plus one guard number that must not get worse (retention or churn next to a conversion number) [S-L19-106] [S-L19-105] [inferred proposal]; check it before and after at minimum; run a controlled test only with enough traffic, test big differences before details, and ship the winner (STD-when-to-animate-22); never claim impact from a five-person test. The first version of this card rested on one freelancer's video [S-L19-038]; the practice of testing against a control now also comes from a paywall consultant [S-L19-106] and an app founder [S-L19-111] on another channel, backed…

cards.title: AI workspace components beyond labels
cards.default: (default + heuristic) For products whose Q-ai-01 answer is `chat` or `presence-mode`: a prompt box with attachment previews, searchable history, streamed output, and the stop, regenerate, edit and copy controls DC-L13-16 already asks for. A memory panel is required whenever the AI keeps memory [S-L19-055]; this fits the house rule to add previews, confirmations and disclaimers to AI features (STD-visual-details-45) [inferred link]. Two points differ from the source and follow DC-L13-16: a step trail may show retrieval steps and citations, but not narrated reasoning presented as an explanation; and confidence labels belong in high-stakes contexts, not under every response. For data products,…

cards.title: The subscription paywall screen: format, trial and reassurance
cards.default: (default + heuristic) For a product that sells a subscription inside its app: show the outcome before the paywall; start with a simple base paywall (a headline, a few bullets, one continue button); add the reassurance line only when the cancel flow is really that easy (DC-L19-36, DC-L13-15); with a trial, show a timeline with the day of the reminder and the day of the first charge; then test radically different formats against that base before testing details [S-L19-104] [S-L19-106]. Trial terms are owner inputs: the interview records them and never invents them (AGENTS.md). Heuristic: "Would this person be surprised by the charge?" If yes, add the timeline and the reminder [inferred from t…

cards.title: Accessibility floor: WCAG 2.2 AA plus the locked house rules
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default `wcag22-aa`, presented as "AA plus the house locks". Offer `wcag22-aa-plus` for money, health and government products [inferred]. Nothing below AA. Rule of thumb: the level question only decides how strict contrast and mouse targets are; touch targets, zoom, motion, transparency, contrast signals and text scaling are not up for choice.

cards.title: Device settings the product always follows, and controls inside the app
cards.block: Foundations > Accessibility > User settings > Device signals and in-app controls
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default: every device signal followed automatically and never asked about; no extra in-app controls unless Q-theme-01 chose a switch or the product serves groups whose needs clash (then personalization). Rule of thumb: if the device already has a switch for it, the product obeys that switch; an in-app control is only for what the device can't express.

cards.title: Mixed input: hover is an extra, press feedback is for everyone
cards.block: Foundations > Interaction > Input capability > Hover and press
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default for Q-plat-03: touch + pointer + keyboard, treated as possibly on the same device, on every web surface; native phone apps are touch plus the operating system's keyboard and switch access [inferred]. Rule of thumb: design the touch version first; hover can only add, never hold something people need.

cards.title: Web product on phones: installed-app feel or scrolling document
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default: derived from Q-scope-01 and shown as a confirm chip: `product-app` gives an app shell, `marketing` or `docs-content` gives a document, both give per surface; PWA only when the person says people will install it. The baseline always ships when phones are in scope. Rule of thumb from the source: own scroll areas, a drawer people drag down, or a canvas means app shell; reading top to bottom means document [S-L19-028].

cards.title: Thumb reach: where frequent actions sit on a phone
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default on phones: bottom-weighted, with navigation and the one or two most frequent actions at the bottom and rare or global actions (settings, notifications, close) at the top; break the main action out of the bar only when it is also the most used; no handedness-specific layout. Rule of thumb: rank actions by how often they are used; the more often, the lower (and, for the one dominant action, the bigger [inferred from S-L19-077]).

cards.title: New interactions: where they may appear and what backs them up
cards.block: Patterns > Interaction > Convention vs novelty > Gestures and signature moments
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default `custom-skin`: gestures only as shortcuts with a visible twin; one signature moment, in onboarding or a rare success state, never in everyday navigation. On native apps that moment lives inside one screen or uses the native stack's own options with `animationMatchesGesture`, never a JavaScript-rebuilt screen transition (STD-mobile-touch-42, STD-mobile-touch-44; DC-L19-90). Rule of thumb: if a newcomer can't find the action without being told, it needs a visible control; if people see the motion 100 or more times a day, it belongs to the platform.

cards.title: What stays native, whatever the look
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default for every posture in React Native: the platform owns navigation, sheets, tabs, menus and pull to refresh; the brand owns the look and the motion inside screens; one press scale on both platforms unless the app is Material-styled. This confirms DC-L10-02's hybrid rule and DC-L06-14's 80/20; in React Native it narrows `brand-first` to "brand look on native behavior" [inferred], while other stacks keep DC-L10-02's options. Rule of thumb: if people's thumbs already know it from every other app, don't rebuild it.

cards.title: Build stack and the house toolkit that comes with it
cards.block: Platforms > Implementation > Build stack and toolkit
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default: React gives the curated list; React Native gives the Expo stack; SwiftUI gives the write-swift standard; any other stack is recorded with a plain note that the house toolkit doesn't cover it. Rule of thumb: read `package.json` first and keep a library the project already has; name one library per job, never a menu.

cards.title: Desktop app: a window people visit, or a presence where they work
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default: a destination window [inferred; the video argues that a native-feeling utility should not be a destination, but most desktop apps are not capture utilities]; add one shortcut panel when the core task happens while people are in other apps, as with capturing inspiration mid-work [S-L19-067] (search and clipboard, after Spotlight and Paste, are [inferred] extensions); ambient pop-ups only for time-bound events such as Notion's meeting pop-up [S-L19-067] [inferred scope]. Rule of thumb: if the task starts in another app, the product should come to that app.

cards.title: Desktop main window: title bar and layout
cards.block: Platforms > Desktop > Window chrome and main-window layout
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default for macOS apps: an integrated title bar with top bar, sidebar and content, and a calm top strip; drop the sidebar when navigation is only browsing and searching [S-L19-067], which sits below DC-L08-19's range of three to five top destinations that a desktop sidebar holds [inferred]. Rule of thumb: the window's top edge belongs to the window, not to actions.

cards.title: Keyboard shortcuts: which actions get them, how people learn them, what they see
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default for desktop and web apps: OS standards untouched; shortcuts for the most frequent actions, shown on their buttons and menu rows; a cheat sheet in settings; feedback as an instant state change, never an animation. Rule of thumb: every shortcut needs a visible result in the frame it fires and a visible place to learn it.

cards.title: Search on desktop: a command palette, or search in place
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default: prominent in-place search for one-screen and content apps; add a ⌘K palette when the product has many sections (about five or more top-level sections [inferred threshold]) or commands that lead elsewhere. Rule of thumb: if most results are destinations, use a palette; if they are items on this screen, filter in place [S-L19-067].

cards.title: Real-device check: which device counts as proof
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default when phones are in scope: at least one physical iPhone and one older Android [inferred pairing; the sources say "a phone that's a few years old" and "slowest supported device"], release builds for native apps, standalone mode for PWAs; emulators only for layout sketches. Rule of thumb: if it hasn't run on a phone, say which parts are unverified instead of calling it done.

cards.title: Asking for system permissions, notifications first
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default `primer`, shown when the permission starts to pay off for the person (after they set a goal, start a trial or ask for a reminder), with a preview when the notification's content is the selling point. "Not now" is respected: the product asks again only when the person turns on a feature that needs the permission, never on a timer, which would be the nagging DC-L13-15 lints [inferred]. Rule of thumb: ask when people can see what they get, and say it in one line (STD-visual-details-41).

cards.title: Store rules and where people pay
cards.block: Platforms > Mobile > App store rules and payment surface
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default `store-only`, recorded as an owner input; web checkout only when the owner confirms their store and market allow it. Rules whatever the choice: avoid a free-trial toggle on an iOS paywall, because Apple began rejecting some in early 2026 [S-L19-104] (one video's dated report, to re-check before relying on it, as DC-L19-106 and DC-L19-139 also say); a web checkout keeps cancelling as easy as subscribing, since DC-L13-15 flags a cancel flow with more steps than sign-up and cites the EU DSA's example of termination made harder than subscribing [inferred application; the source does not say whether harder cancelling explains any of Stripe's higher LTV]; a discount …

cards.title: Accounts on phones: none, the platform's sign-in, or an email account
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default: start with the founder's question, why does this product need an account at all [S-L19-111]. No account while the device can keep the data and nothing has to sync; when an account is needed, offer the platform's sign-in first and, when the core can run without an account, ask after people have felt the product [S-L19-107] [inferred ranking]; ask for an email only with the reason in view (STD-visual-details-41). Rule of thumb: an account has to earn its screen.

cards.title: The Swift token file: where it lives and how it is isolated
cards.block: Platforms > Implementation > Swift and SwiftUI output
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default: the token file marked `nonisolated` wherever it goes; in the app target while there is one app, in a package once a second target needs it [inferred]; the Swift version recorded with Q-plat-09 before any Swift is written (STD-swift-01). Rule of thumb: tokens are constants, and constants should be readable from any code.

cards.title: Sharing out of the app: the system share, share cards and the screenshot moment
cards.block: Platforms > Sharing > How content leaves the app
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default `system-share` on anything a person might send; share cards only when the product's data says something about the person (recaps, progress, results); the screenshot flow only when people already screenshot those moments [inferred]. Rule of thumb: people share what says something about them [S-L19-111]; Mobbin's gut check for memorable dashboards, "Would I screenshot this, and why?" [S-L19-110], can also pick which screens deserve a share card [inferred application].

cards.title: Which references to learn from, and what to take from each
cards.block: Builder > Input > Reference intake (Stage 00; also Stage 03 product likes)
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default: ask for products the person uses first. Accept a showcase shot, but say it is read for mood only, not for layout or values [S-L19-086] [S-L19-068]. Heuristic: for every reference, ask one follow-up, "What do you like about it?", and record the answer as its reason, because taste means naming why something feels right [S-L19-008] [S-L19-011]. Take structure section by section, never identity (confirms DC-L17-03 and Q-ref-01's use/avoid line). Confirms DC-L18-09 (1-3 references liked and one disliked). Second heuristic: for each element carried over from a reference, ask why this product needs it. Moonly's founder asks that before copying anything other apps hav…

cards.title: Naming the feeling: one target emotion, shown as one layout in different flavors
cards.block: Foundations > Brand > Personality > Target emotion (Stage 03, with the zoom 0 "how should it feel?" question)
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default: at zoom 0, pick one lead emotion from the person's feel words and say it back in one line ("I read that as calm"), then record it. At zoom 2, show the person's own sample screen in two or three flavors of the same layout, one at a time and full size (as DC-L19-34 and DC-L19-56 already require for type and layout). Heuristic: when two sliders pull a value in opposite directions, the lead emotion breaks the tie [inferred]. Treat the slider-to-token matrix as a starting point and judge the result for feeling: the video chooses each part of an identity for the feeling it gives, not from a formula [S-L19-062], and that a matrix alone can give a soulless result is […

cards.title: How design principles are worded and used
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Keep `generate` as the default (3-5 principles, each naming what it outranks, one making accessibility non-negotiable). Add two standing lines to every generated set: a familiarity rule and a purpose rule. Use Apple's eight as the vocabulary the builder reasons with when it explains a recommendation, not as the product's own principles. This differs from DC-L11-05 in kind, not in substance: DC-L11-05 warns against generic words every product could claim ("simple", "beautiful") as the product's principles; the eight are a shared reasoning vocabulary, so they sit beside the product's specific set rather than replacing it [inferred].

cards.title: How much system this team needs
cards.block: Delivery > Governance > System size (Stage 25, and the "stop here or zoom in" offer)
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default: for one person or a small team building one product, recommend stopping at zoom 1 plus the areas they care about, and skip stage 25's zoom 3 questions [inferred: the sources say to size the system to the team, not which zoom level to stop at]. Say why in plain words: a system is a few decisions held everywhere, not a component count [S-L19-044] [S-L19-054]. Recommend deep definition only when several products or teams share the system [inferred from S-L19-054's Material example]. This confirms DC-L11-03's strict core for teams and adds size as its own dial, separate from strictness [inferred]. Invest in excellent defaults before adding options (STD-visual-deta…

cards.title: Breaking a rule on purpose: how exceptions are recorded and reviewed
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default: every exception carries a one-line reason. The review lists reasoned exceptions under "kept on purpose" and does not count them as findings; an ignore with no reason is itself a finding. This covers project rules (tokens, patterns, the person's decisions) only: a reason never waives a house standard, which changes only through `engine.py standard override` with the owner's words (the standards policy), and never waives an accessibility floor. Heuristic: when the same exception appears three times, it is a missing token or a rule to change, not an exception [inferred]. Agents follow the same rule: when the builder or another agent departs from a system rule or …

cards.title: How you will know the system helped
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default for one person or a small team: one product result they already track (sign-ups, sales or a key task), compared before and after, plus a findability check on the main screen. Add adoption measures (DC-L11-20) once more than one team uses the system. Heuristic: a small pre-launch test finds problems; it does not prove impact [S-L19-038]; a controlled test with enough traffic can [S-L19-111], and only then (agrees with DC-L19-137). The before-and-after advice comes from one freelancer's video [S-L19-038]; it agrees with DC-L11-20 that success needs measuring, but it targets product outcomes rather than system adoption.

cards.title: What the builder's checks cannot judge
cards.block: Delivery > Quality > Checks by hand (Stage 25; the end of `engine.py review`)
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default: every `engine.py review` ends with a short "check by hand" list drawn from what changed: motion gets slow motion and a reduced-motion toggle, gestures get a physical phone, type gets a look on the target screen, and the product's main screen gets the screenshot question with its "why" written down [S-L19-110] [inferred]. Nothing that depends on feel is reported as verified [S-L19-016] [S-L19-028]. Heuristic: if it moves or answers a touch, it needs a hand check [inferred].

cards.title: How the decisions are written up for other people
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Keep RATIONALE.md to one page, in the case-study shape: open with the problem and a one-line answer; place a small rendered sample (the chosen option beside its main alternative) next to each of the five choices; close with "What we'd do next", covering open items and what was left out. Heuristic: if a reason can't be written in one sentence, the decision isn't settled yet [inferred]. Confirms DC-L17-10 and DC-L11-12. The case-study advice comes from portfolio videos for job seekers [S-L19-083] [S-L19-064]; using it for a design system's rationale is [inferred].

cards.title: Docs people can touch: demos, good-and-bad pairs, snippets and a changelog
cards.block: Delivery > Documentation > Page content (Stage 26; also the Stage 25 change-communication question)
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default: every generated page gets one live demo, one good-and-bad pair wherever the system has a rule, a copy button for code and another for markdown, and the docs site gets a changelog page. Confirms DC-L11-18's page template and Q-dist-04's default; adds the pair and the copy-as-markdown button.

cards.title: Who sees the result, and how it is framed
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default: the preview opens in the deciding view; the client and showcase framings are extra exports [inferred]. Heuristic: match the frame to the audience, and keep showcase tricks out of client meetings, where they work less well [S-L19-041]. Differs from DC-L16-06 (a split view with a component matrix and 2-4 sample screens, every mode at once) only when options are being compared: the chosen system can still be shown that way, but competing options are shown one at a time, full size (STD-process-review-taste-43) [inferred]. cards.block: Delivery > AI channels > Agent rule files (Stage 26)
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default: keep DESIGN.md and DTCG files, and add one short rule file per aspect, generated from the person's decisions and the house standards, each rule strict and with its reason. cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default: taste tells warn and can be kept on purpose with a reason (DC-L19-165); a look the person chose, such as a centered hero for a single statement, is not flagged. Tells that break a house standard are not waivable by a reason comment: ease-in on UI motion (STD-easing-duration-03), a solid border where a semi-transparent shadow fits (STD-visual-details-14), motion that runs but feels mediocre (STD-process-review-taste-01) and placeholder copy or dead buttons in prototypes (STD-process-review-taste-40) keep being flagged until fixed, and change only when the owner overrides the standard with `engine.py standard override` (DC-L19-165). cards.title: What the Figma copy contains so designers can keep working in it
cards.block: Delivery > Output > Figma library (Stage 26, the push to Figma)
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default: follow DC-L07-21 (variables for values, including colors by mode; styles for bundles). Build every generated component on auto layout, keep part names identical across variants and states so multi-edit and Smart Animate work, and add a states frame per interactive component. "Styles for colors" comes from one June 2025 video of beginner mistakes [S-L19-045], which gives no reason for it; DC-L07-21 holds because colors change between light and dark.

cards.title: How variations are generated and compared
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default: replace `show-6` with a picker of 3 named directions on different axes, one at a time and full size in the real preview, with a table of when each is right and its cost; the person picks. If asked which the builder would pick, it answers from the product's personality and how often the thing is used, not from looks alone [S-L19-031]. Lock and shuffle stays for tuning inside the chosen direction, showing one result at a time [inferred]. Differs from DC-L16-05 (the "show 6" grid) and from DC-L17-05's upper option of 8 (gstack); the standards cap variants at 5. DC-L17-05's light and dark side by side compares one variant in two modes, not variants, so it can stay…

cards.title: How AI edits and fine-tuning happen
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default: patches with before and after (confirms DC-L16-04), plus a temporary on-page control for values that need the eye (positions, as in the source [S-L19-103]; widths in characters and opacity, which the source tuned by trying values in prompts, are [inferred] candidates), with every tuned value saved as a decision with the person's reason. Heuristic: fix one named issue at a time, in place; regenerate only when the direction itself is wrong [S-L19-045] [inferred]. The workflow is one designer's live session [S-L19-103], a practice rather than a tested method.

cards.title: How a critique or review is reported
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default: `engine.py review` prints one table (Where, Before, After, Why), where Why names the standard or decision and its reason, each row with one severity and the rows ordered by leverage (STD-process-review-taste-09, -10), followed by a one-line verdict ("ready" or "fix N before shipping"). Any review that covers motion ends with Block or Approve under the stated criteria in every mode, because STD-process-review-taste-05 requires it; strict mode also uses Block or Approve for the rest of the review [inferred]. Coach mode uses the same row format in chat. Confirms DC-L15-11's rule that every message names the principle.

cards.title: The goal behind the brief, before any visuals
cards.block: Foundations > Product > Goal and user intent (Stage 03, beside the principles; `PRODUCT.md`)
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default: at zoom 0, take the goal from the person's first answer when it is there; otherwise ask one short follow-up: "What should people get done first when they arrive?" Record it; previews use it to pick the sample screen. Heuristic: a section, component or principle that serves neither the goal nor an intent is a candidate to cut [S-L19-020] [S-L19-054]; Moonly asked the same of its login screen and removed it [S-L19-111]. cards.block: Builder > AI > Pattern research before a flow is drafted (Stage 27; feeds Stage 00 and the stage 23 patterns)
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default: before drafting a flow with domain rules (sign-up and account opening, checkout and payments, onboarding), the builder compares how a few shipped products in the same industry and on the same platform handle it. cards.title: Launch and share surfaces: what the system covers outside the product
cards.block: Delivery > Launch > Store pages, share images and launch material (Stage 26; Q-scope-01's surfaces)
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Default: the system covers the product's own surfaces until the person names a launch, a store listing or sharing. Then it adds three templates built from the same tokens: a share image for the product's one shareable moment, a store and showcase screenshot frame that shows what the product does and what to do next, and launch visuals built around the signature interaction [S-L19-006] [S-L19-110] [S-L19-111] (bundling them is [inferred]).
